interpretation_notes: The surrendered-KMT stay-neutral sentence belongs to the preceding CCP/Dadao-attack paragraph of RB4.9. The foreign-invasion paragraph and table supply automatic/die KMT outcomes without that exception, and adopted RCL-003 preserves the automatic KMT outcome. Apply that result to actual surviving warlord land and units even after KMT surrendered, ending its no-land condition; do not restore erased resources or reset one-time awards. This is a source-combination inference, not a new user ruling. Direct CCP/Dadao attacks still leave the warlord neutral when KMT has surrendered.

source_refs.section: 4.9 explicit exception limited to CCP/Dadao attacks

interpretation_notes: RB104/105 and the adopted RCL-002 natural-12 outcome have no surrender exception. RB5.7 forbids liberation to a surrendered nation, not alignment. RB4.9 expressly leaves a warlord neutral after a CCP/Dadao attack when KMT has surrendered; that attack-only exception is not applied to an influence backfire. Alignment supplies actual land/units, ending KMT’s no-land surrender condition. Reactivation is this source-combination inference, not an expressly printed KMT revival sentence or a new user ruling.

The general Minor-to-Major alignment rule incorporates the minor, except for named CCP/KMT/Free France exceptions. Mongolia’s specific printed alignment recipient is USSR, and the campaign disables that absent-nation alignment while retaining Mongolia’s identity. A common enemy with CCP therefore does not invent a separate non-incorporating Mongolia/CCP alignment or its shared access/defense permissions.
